items.title: A stolen iPhone, $14,000 in losses and London's crypto theft problem
items.description: Two strangers befriended Magnus Ahmad outside a London bar. Hours later, thieves had emptied his crypto wallets, accessed his bank accounts and disabled his laptop.

items.title: Traders are already placing leveraged bets on Anthropic’s IPO using crypto contracts
items.description: Trade.xyz’s new ANT contract fell about 20% in its first hour on Hyperliquid. There are no shares behind it, and U.S. traders are locked out.

items.title: Binance says it has replaced 90% of stolen crypto after massive $6.3 billion breach
items.description: Binance is absorbing all losses through corporate funds, futures reserves, and SAFU, keeping user balances intact.

items.title: Institutions embrace crypto staking despite shrinking yields
items.description: Easier access and growing familiarity are encouraging investors to stake their tokens, while falling rewards and withdrawal delays test the economics.

items.title: Uber tests how tokenization can put idle cash to work with HSBC, Franklin Templeton
items.description: The pilot let Uber keep funds invested in money market products while accessing cash for payments, even on weekends.

items.title: As big bitcoin miners chase AI profits, individuals get another shot at the rewards
items.description: Several companies offer access to bitcoin mining without the hassle of running equipment, but high costs and the 2028 reward halving make profits uncertain.

items.title: 18 years in, what has Bitcoin truly done?
items.description: The Bitcoin white paper achieved a lot of what Satoshi Nakamoto set out to accomplish, but the cultural impact it had may outweigh Bitcoin itself, writes CoinDesk's Nikhilesh De.

items.title: A Nasdaq-listed company may sell $450 million bitcoin, citing Binance hack and quantum fears
items.description: Next Technology Holding cited exchange security and quantum computing risks in authorizing sales or loans against its 5,833 BTC. It says none of the coins are held at Binance.

items.title: Binance says 90% of stolen assets replenished, targets Sunday withdrawals
items.description: Less-liquid tokens make up the remaining shortfall as Binance continues buying replacement assets through market and over-the-counter trades.

items.title: Bitcoin held up better than expected after Binance hack, Strive CEO says
items.description: Strive CEO Matt Cole says the Binance hack has not changed his long-term case for Bitcoin, but cautions it is too early to call a market bottom.

items.title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
items.description: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.

items.title: Bitcoin turns 18: Has the original rebel grown up?
items.description: In typical Bitcoin style, the number one cryptocurrency turns 18 today, amid AI-driven security threats, quantum fears and the biggest exchange hack in crypto history.

items.title: Texas brothers sentenced to 15 years in prison for armed crypto robbery, kidnapping
items.description: Home invasions became the most common form of crypto wrench attacks worldwide during the first half of 2026, rising to 20 incidents from one.

items.title: Blockchain investigator Chainalysis hit by cybersecurity incident
items.description: The company said some non-sensitive customer data was exposed, including user IDs, names and email addresses.

items.title: Binance $6.3B record hack sparks pre-election political clashes
items.description: Some political and administration figures tried to make hay of the biggest-ever crypto heist.

items.title: Binance hackers raced to move billions before it could be frozen
items.description: Attackers raced to convert stolen stablecoins into crypto that issuers could not freeze as industry players like Tether and Circle moved to immobilize billions of dollars in assets.

items.title: Trump promised to slash energy costs — but gasoline, diesel and jet fuel all soared instead
items.description: President Donald Trump promised voters who were angry about inflation that he would slash gasoline prices below $2 a gallon in his first year in office.

items.title: Binance says 90% of $6.3 billion hack losses are now covered, plans to resume withdrawals Sunday
items.description: Binance says it has restored backing for 90% of assets affected by its $6.3 billion hack and is planning to resume withdrawals, subject to security checks.

items.title: ‘Pop-up’ super PACs pour $637 million into 2026 midterm races
items.description: Twenty-two late-forming super PACs spent about $637 million in 2026 congressional races, sometimes before voters could see their donors.

items.title: Automakers like Rivian and Ford are ‘democratizing 3D printing’ to reduce costs and increase speed
items.description: Automakers including Ford, Rivian and GM are expanding 3D printing to make prototypes, factory tools and low-volume parts faster and at lower cost.

items.title: Anthropic's path to the Nasdaq just got a lot bumpier
items.description: Concerning projections from hyperscalers this week punished tech stocks and pushed the Nasdaq to its first three-week losing streak since March.

items.description: Two high-profile security incidents this week, including the largest crypto theft in history, have raised custody and safety concerns.

items.title: Humans are still doing the work behind some AI agents
items.description: AI agents from startups including Dazzle, Duckbill and Wajo still rely on human workers for calls and other real-world tasks when software falls short.
